whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should take the Tableau Consultant exam?

personas.label: Analytics consultants
personas.description: You deliver Tableau projects for clients and want a credential for consulting work.

personas.label: Business intelligence project leads
personas.description: You manage data sources, dashboards, publishing, and user adoption.

personas.label: Solution architects
personas.description: You design how Tableau fits within a client’s wider data environment.

examDifficulty.heading: How challenging is the Tableau Consultant exam?
examDifficulty.summary: This exam covers end-to-end Tableau delivery, not only view creation. It tests how you gather needs, prepare data, build useful dashboards, and publish and govern content on Tableau Cloud or Server.
bullets: 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
63% to pass, which is 38 correct answers out of 60.
Full delivery lifecycle. Expect discovery, data prep, publishing, access, and adoption.
Client judgement. Several choices may work, but select the one that best fits the stated audience and constraints.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Practise turning a broad request into a data source and dashboard, publishing it with suitable access, and explaining your decisions. Aim for 75% or higher on practice tests.

examFormat.heading: Tableau Consultant exam format
examFormat.intro: The proctored exam is available online or at a test centre. Many questions ask how to respond to a client situation.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Scenarios may describe an unused dashboard, a shared data source that performs poorly, or another client challenge. Choose the next step that addresses the stated need.
bestWayToPass: Start with the business question: The audience and decision determine the data and visualization.
Prepare data upstream: Know when Tableau Prep is a better fit than repeating transformations in workbooks.
Use published sources: A governed source reused across workbooks can prevent conflicting definitions.
Plan adoption: Training, subscriptions, and alerts can be as important as the dashboard itself.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers the delivery of Tableau solutions, from discovery and data preparation to dashboard design, publishing, governance, and adoption. The exam is 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, with a 63% pass mark, weighted towards Design and Troubleshoot Calculations and Workbooks (40%) and Evaluate Current State (22%).

blocks.heading: Discover needs and define the solution
blocks.body: Begin by finding the decision the client needs to make. Ask who will use the result, how current the data must be, and what process they follow today. These answers shape the design: executives may need a few clear measures, while analysts may need filters and detail. Agree on measure definitions in writing to avoid disputes later. Decide whether logic belongs in the source system, Tableau Prep, a published data source, or a workbook.

blocks.heading: Prepare data with Tableau Prep
blocks.body: Tableau Prep Builder cleans and reshapes data before it reaches a workbook. Steps can clean values, rename or split fields, filter records, change data types, join or union tables, aggregate, and pivot columns into rows. You can output the result as an extract or publish it as a source. Doing shared preparation upstream lets multiple workbooks use the same logic. Prep flows can run on a schedule to keep outputs current.

blocks.heading: Publish and govern shared sources
blocks.body: A published data source on Tableau Cloud or Server can be reused by many workbooks. It can include joins, calculations, field names, descriptions, and permissions. This helps prevent different workbooks from defining a measure in different ways. Certification signals that a source is reviewed and trusted. Set refresh timing according to freshness needs; an extract reduces repeated source queries but is current only after its last refresh, while a live connection queries the source directly.

blocks.heading: Design dashboards for their users
blocks.body: Design for the audience and the device. Lead with the key finding, then provide breakdowns and detail. Actions can let a selection in one view filter or highlight another. Keep filters focused because they take attention and can affect performance. Size the dashboard for the screen people will use. Apply color deliberately to guide attention, and consider separate focused dashboards when audiences need different levels of detail.

blocks.heading: Publish, manage access, and support adoption
blocks.body: Tableau Cloud and Server organize content in projects. Manage permissions by group at the project level where possible, and decide who can view, edit, or publish. Subscriptions send a view on a schedule; data-driven alerts notify users when a measure crosses a threshold. Launch to a small group, review usage, and respond to early feedback. A dashboard that people do not use has not delivered its intended value.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the Tableau Consultant exam
scenarioTips.intro: Choose the answer that best fits the client’s audience, data, and constraints, even when other options could also work.

blocks.heading: Start with discovery
blocks.body: Identify the audience, the decision to support, required data freshness, and the current process before selecting a design.

blocks.heading: Place transformations for reuse
blocks.body: Prefer the source system, then Tableau Prep, then a published data source, and finally workbook logic when it must be view-specific.

blocks.heading: Use governed data sources
blocks.body: A shared, trusted source helps keep measures consistent across workbooks.

blocks.heading: Design for the audience
blocks.body: Show the key finding first, limit filters, use color with care, and size dashboards for the device viewers use.

blocks.heading: Check adoption
blocks.body: Subscriptions and alerts can bring users back. Start with a small launch group, review usage, and address feedback.

sampleQuestions.question: Five workbooks calculate revenue differently, so teams disagree in meetings. What should the consultant recommend?
options: Train each team to write calculations
One certified source
Change all connections from extracts to live
Rebuild each workbook independently
sampleQuestions.explanation: One governed source with the agreed definition prevents workbooks from calculating revenue differently. Certification marks it as trusted.
whyWrong: Training does not keep separate calculations aligned over time.
Connection type does not determine how revenue is defined.
Separate rebuilds preserve the same risk of inconsistent definitions.

sampleQuestions.question: Monthly sales values are spread across twelve columns, one for each month. What is a clean way to reshape the data?
options: Create twelve calculations in every workbook
Publish twelve separate data sources
Ask users to re-enter the data in a new layout
Pivot month columns into rows in Prep
sampleQuestions.explanation: Pivoting converts the monthly columns into rows, a structure that is easier to analyze and can be reused across workbooks.
whyWrong: Twelve workbook calculations repeat the transformation.
Many sources make maintenance harder.
Manual re-entry is error-prone and does not scale.

sampleQuestions.question: An executive dashboard is crowded and slow, with fifteen filters. What should the consultant do first?
options: Move it to a larger server
Focus on executives’ key measures
Add further filters so users can narrow results
Replace every chart with a table
sampleQuestions.explanation: Reducing the dashboard to the measures executives need can improve clarity and reduce work.
whyWrong: Hardware does not fix a crowded design.
More filters add clutter and may increase query cost.
Tables may make results harder to scan and do not address excess content.

sampleQuestions.question: Sales leaders need an alert when a region’s weekly revenue drops below target. Which feature fits?
options: Hold a weekly meeting to inspect the dashboard
Send the entire dashboard to everyone each morning
Add a note to the dashboard title
Create a data-driven alert on the revenue measure
sampleQuestions.explanation: A data-driven alert can notify users when a measure crosses a defined threshold.
whyWrong: A meeting depends on someone noticing the change and is not timely.
A scheduled subscription sends whether or not the threshold is crossed.
Static text cannot respond to changing data.

sampleQuestions.question: Where should permissions usually be managed on Tableau Cloud or Server?
options: Export dashboards as PDFs for all users
Set them individually on every workbook
Use group permissions at the project level
Share a common user account and password
sampleQuestions.explanation: Group permissions at the project level are easier to manage as users and content change.
whyWrong: PDF exports lose interactivity and may become outdated.
Per-user settings on each workbook are difficult to maintain.
Shared accounts weaken security and accountability.

sampleQuestions.question: The client asks for “real-time” reporting, but its warehouse loads new data nightly. What should the consultant do first?
options: Use a manual spreadsheet upload
Refresh an extract every five minutes
Clarify how fresh the data needs to be
Switch to live and promise real-time data
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Tableau connection cannot make the underlying source fresher than its nightly update, so clarify the business need.
whyWrong: Manual uploads add effort and are not more current.
Frequent refreshes of unchanged data waste resources.
A live connection still reads data that updates only nightly.

sampleQuestions.question: Most viewers will use a dashboard on tablets while working in the field. What should the consultant consider?
options: Design and size the dashboard for tablet use
Add many more worksheets
Use a fixed 4K layout
Assume the desktop design will always resize well
sampleQuestions.explanation: The dashboard should be planned for the screen and conditions in which people will use it.
whyWrong: More worksheets make the experience harder on a small screen.
A 4K layout is not suited to a tablet.
Automatic resizing may not produce a usable layout.

sampleQuestions.question: Why perform shared data cleanup in Tableau Prep rather than repeating it in workbook calculations?
options: It removes the need to configure permissions
Reuse prepared data across workbooks
It makes every workbook file larger
It automatically converts live connections to extracts
sampleQuestions.explanation: Preparing data upstream makes the transformation consistent for all workbooks that use the output.
whyWrong: Published content still needs appropriate permissions.
File size is not the benefit of using Prep.
Connection type is a separate configuration choice.

sampleQuestions.question: After six months, very few users open a dashboard. What should the consultant investigate first?
options: Check whether it answers a user need
Whether more charts should be added
Whether the colors match the brand
Whether the client should buy more licenses
sampleQuestions.explanation: Low usage may mean the dashboard does not answer a question users need to act on. Revisit the original need.
whyWrong: More charts may add clutter without making the dashboard useful.
Brand colors are unlikely to explain whether a tool supports a decision.
More licenses do not increase adoption by themselves.

sampleQuestions.question: A client needs executive summaries, regional analysis, and rep-level details. What is a better design approach?
options: Create several nearly identical dashboards with saved filters
Put every chart and level of detail on one dashboard
Create focused dashboards for each audience and link them
Display all data in one large crosstab
sampleQuestions.explanation: Separate focused dashboards can serve each audience clearly and are easier to maintain than a crowded or duplicated design.
whyWrong: Near-identical copies increase maintenance work.
One dashboard may overwhelm users with different needs.
A large crosstab is difficult to scan and may perform poorly.

sampleQuestions.question: What does certification of a published data source tell users?
options: It refreshes faster than other sources
Its contents are encrypted
Only administrators may access it
Mark it as reviewed and trusted
sampleQuestions.explanation: Certification marks a source as reviewed and approved for users to prefer.
whyWrong: Certification does not change refresh performance.
It is not an encryption setting.
Certified sources can be used by authorized users beyond administrators.

sampleQuestions.question: Stakeholders use different definitions of “active customer.” What should the consultant do before building?
options: Build one definition and wait for feedback
Agree on a definition and document it
Show both measures in the same chart
Use the most senior stakeholder’s preferred definition
sampleQuestions.explanation: Agreeing and recording the definition before building avoids rework and conflicting results.
whyWrong: Building before agreement risks rework.
Two competing measures can confuse the audience.
Seniority alone does not resolve the business definition.

sampleQuestions.question: A published extract takes two hours and finishes after the morning meeting. What is a sensible first optimization?
options: Reduce rows and fields, then aggregate
Change all users to live connections
Move the meeting later
Schedule the extract to run more often
sampleQuestions.explanation: Reducing unnecessary extract data can shorten refresh time before changing infrastructure or schedules.
whyWrong: Live connections may place more load on the source.
Changing the meeting schedule avoids the technical problem.
More frequent runs of a slow extract can create a larger queue.

sampleQuestions.question: Which order generally favors putting reusable transformation logic as far upstream as possible?
options: Workbook, published source, Prep, then source system
Let each developer choose independently
Source, Prep, published source, workbook
Keep every calculation in the workbook
sampleQuestions.explanation: Logic placed earlier can be reused by more downstream consumers and is less likely to diverge.
whyWrong: This order starts with workbook logic and increases duplication.
A consistent placement strategy supports reuse better than individual preference.
Workbook-only logic is difficult for other workbooks to reuse.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a Tableau Cloud or Server subscription do?
options: Emails a view to users on a schedule
Marks a data source as certified
Refreshes an extract
Gives a user permission to edit a workbook
sampleQuestions.explanation: A subscription sends a view by email at a chosen time or schedule.
whyWrong: Certification signals trust in a data source.
Extract refreshes are scheduled separately.
Editing access is controlled through permissions.
